# libwebsockets / fuzz-gif

libwebsockets's own fuzz target `fuzz-gif` ([source](source/main.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libwebsockets (warmcat/libwebsockets at 1b5cc65f).

First byte selects hold_at_metadata; the rest is fed to the stateful GIF decoder (lws_gif_emit_next_line) line by line until OK/FATAL/stall, then lws_gif_restart and a second full pass; return codes only steer the loop, pixels are not checked (the two passes are not compared).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libwebsockets at commit 1b5cc65f.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libwebsockets` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
